doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Playing avant-garde in New Orleans: the last free man
summary: Jordan calls it terrible; he started the IAQ with Alvin Fielder, was uninvited from the jazz festival, and has communities elsewhere including the AACM.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Well what’s it like trying to play what we’ll call — for lack of a better term — avante garde in New Orleans.

Terrible. I’ve been there. They had — somebody wrote an article on me maybe about eight or ten years ago and said I’m the last free man in New Orleans. And the other day my house was flooded and I happened to run across all that and I sort of picked it up because I had my little grandson, he was a little boy, standing on the side of me. Me and Fred Anderson had played a gig in New Orleans that day and somebody wrote an article saying I was the last free man standing. And my little grandson, he was a little bit of a — so it’s hard, see ‘cause Clyde and all of them came up under me. They came up, I’ve had the free — me and Al Fielder, the drummer, Alvin Fielder, we started the IAQ. But there’s been a lot of kids that came through SUNO and we’ve always had free bands but they don’t, not too many of them play like that because they can’t get any work. So I guess I’m just one of them that was just so pig-headed that I just wanted to keep it going so it’s just hard to do. And this year — I played every festival in New Orleans and this year they didn’t invite me. I didn’t play this year on the last jazz festival. So maybe I might have been the last free man or the last one standing ‘cause Katrina may have wiped all of that out and wiped me out too. But you know the thing about it, I’ve got communities all over, I’ve got communities in California, Chicago, New York and Europe. So you know I can deal with that. I just got a call today. The cat asks me to come and play with the AACM, just come in solo with the AACM, just come in, just like I do, just get your horn out and walk on the stand and play with us. And we had a good festival in San Jose last week and it was very good. So there’s other communities that is opening up. And then I’m getting old, so, older you know, at that age, but I’m really getting old so maybe I need to stop a little bit and just smell the roses.
